records.name: SEPTA Toastmasters
records.summary: A Toastmasters club that meets at lunchtime at SEPTA headquarters on Market Street, in person or online, to practice public speaking. Visits are free, and guests do not have to speak until they are ready.
records.what_you_do: Practice short speeches at lunchtime meetings, and take meeting roles such as timer or evaluator.

schedule.text: Meets on the 2nd and 4th Wednesday of the month from noon to 1 pm, except December. Meetings are in person at SEPTA headquarters or online.

locations.label: SEPTA Headquarters, Market Street (room number to confirm when you sign up)

cost.text: Visits are listed as free. Membership dues are $70 every six months.

first_step.how: Email the club at least 48 hours before the meeting to register as a guest, using Toastmasters@septa.org, then come to a noon meeting in person or ask for the online link.
first_step.basis: The club says guests are welcome at any meeting and gives a clear way to sign up ahead by email. The club pages do not say whether guests must speak.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each meeting runs from noon to 1 pm on the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays, in person at SEPTA headquarters or online. The club pages do not say whether guests must speak or how a meeting runs for visitors, so ask when you register. Visits are listed as free, and membership dues are $70 every six months.
first_visit_tips: Email the club at least 48 hours before the meeting, since building security needs advance notice of guests.
Bring a government-issued photo ID on the day of your visit.
Ask which room to go to, because the club's pages list two different room numbers.
If you would rather join from home, ask for the online meeting link when you register.

records.notes: Guest sign up email conflict: the guests page names SeptaToast@gmail.com, while the home and directions pages name Toastmasters@septa.org. The record uses the second. Room conflict: the home page says Room 11C and the directions page says Room 8A, so the label asks visitors to confirm. No upcoming meeting is posted and the contact page says the next meeting date is to be announced, so confirm a meeting is scheduled before going. The phone number 215-580-7036 comes from the tier 1 Toastmasters listing; the club site shows no phone. The club's visitor counter in the footer is not evidence of activity. No SEPTA stop is named on the club pages. A web search suggested 13th Street station, but no club page names it, so nearest stop is left out.

records.name: Serve Philadelphia VISTA Corps
records.summary: Places full time AmeriCorps VISTA members for a year of paid, stipend supported national service inside City offices, for example the Office of Immigrant Affairs.
records.what_you_do: Serve a full year inside a City department on one project, such as building language access tools, writing a community resource guide, or organizing volunteer events for Community Schools.

schedule.text: A one year, full time service term. Applications are closed for now, and the City's interest form is how people hear when the next cycle opens. The start month is not published.

locations.label: City offices, such as the Office of Immigrant Affairs in City Hall

first_step.how: Fill out the City's interest form to be told when the next VISTA cycle opens, and read the benefits and requirements page. Questions go to ServeVISTA@phila.gov or (215) 686-0823.
first_step.basis: You must apply to join, and the current application window is closed. The City says the roles are entry level and encourages people to apply even if they feel underqualified.
first_step.what_to_expect: Members work full time for one year inside a City department on a project, and the City describes the roles as entry level. The pages read do not list the pay, benefits, eligibility rules, or start month, so ask the contact or read the benefits and requirements page before you apply.
first_visit_tips: Read the benefits and requirements page before you fill out anything.
Expect the window to be closed for now; the last window we found ended April 30, 2025.
Ask the contact about eligibility and the start month, since the public pages do not give them.

records.notes: Tier 1 said a new class starts in late summer and gave a 2026-08 last sign of life tied to a September 2025 article. Neither holds on the pages read, so both were corrected. Stipend amounts, eligibility rules and the benefits and requirements page were not read; the 'paid, stipend supported' wording in the summary is carried from tier 1 and is not confirmed by these pages. The April 2025 page says applications for the 2025 to 2026 corps closed April 30, 2025.

records.name: Settlement Music School
records.summary: A music school with several Philadelphia branches. Adults can take individual lessons, group classes, and ensembles, including jazz, piano, and rock.
records.what_you_do: Take a group class or join an ensemble with other adults, or book individual lessons at a branch.

schedule.text: Adult classes run 10 to 16 weeks at a time, and ensembles run through the school year. The adult class pages do not list days or times, and staff match you to a class at a registration appointment.

locations.label: Mary Louise Curtis Branch (group piano meets in the Helen Eaton Keyboard Lab)

cost.text: Tuition is charged. Adult classes are listed at $330 for 10 weeks (intro piano and guitar), $630 for 16 weeks (group piano), and $265 for 10 weeks (musicianship). Individual lessons are $45 for a half hour, $67.50 for 45 minutes, or $90 for an hour, each week. The registration fee is $65 for one person or $95 for a family, and it is not refundable.

first_step.how: Fill out the inquiry form on the site or call 215-320-2601. A branch staff member will set a phone or video appointment, then a registration appointment to recommend a class and sign you up.
first_step.basis: The adult page says the school welcomes all ages and skill levels, from beginners up, and the enrollment page lays out a clear way to start.
first_step.what_to_expect: You start with a phone or video call with a branch staff member about your interests and goals. At a registration appointment, staff suggest a class, teacher, or program, and you pay the registration fee and first payment to enroll. Group classes are paid as a deposit and installments through the school year.
first_visit_tips: Think about your goals and the instrument or style you want before the first call.
Have a payment method ready: the school takes cash, check, Visa, MasterCard, and debit cards.
Check the hours for the branch you choose, since each branch keeps its own schedule.

records.notes: Branch emails are on the enrollment page but were not recorded; the general info address is used. Settlement Music Online (215-320-2623) has no street address, so it is not listed as a location; online_ok is true. The tuition page covers 2026 to 2027; the classes page states no year. The last sign of life of 2026-05 is the press kit upload month shown on the adult page. The tuition page says financial aid runs through high school (to age 23 for voice students), so no adult aid is recorded. Willow Grove is in Montgomery County, so in_city is false for that branch.

records.name: Shakespeare in Clark Park
records.summary: A theater company that puts on Shakespeare plays outdoors in Clark Park each summer. Audiences come to the shows, and the company posts job openings for artists on its site.
records.what_you_do: Come to a free outdoor show in Clark Park. The company posts paid artist openings under Work with Us, and its site does not describe volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Outdoor summer productions in Clark Park, with evening shows that start at 7 pm.

locations.label: Clark Park, the Bowl (near Chester Avenue and 43rd Street)

cost.text: Shows are described as free on the company's About page. The site also has a donate button.

first_step.how: Check shakespeareinclarkpark.org for the next season's dates, then come to an evening show at the Bowl in Clark Park.
first_step.basis: Shows are free outdoor performances anyone can walk up to. The site does not describe seating, what a first visit is like, or a welcome for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: The 2026 Hamlet ran about 90 minutes with no intermission and started at 7 pm at the Bowl. The company describes picnic style audiences, but the site does not say whether seats are provided. If weather forces a move, that evening's show goes indoors at Plays & Players Theatre, and the company says the show goes on rain or shine.
first_visit_tips: If it rains, check whether the show has moved to Plays & Players Theatre at 1714 Delancey St that evening.
Bring something to sit on if you want it, since the site does not say whether seats are provided.
Find the Bowl near Chester Avenue and 43rd Street, which is where the shows are held.

records.notes: The contact name Kittson Oneill came from the cultural fund directory and tax records, not from the company site, which names no contact person. It was left out of contacts; restore it only if the owner decides it may be published. The Plan Your Visit page names no SEPTA stop, and a guessed directions URL returned 404, so no nearest stop is given. The Hamlet dates (July 29 to August 2, 2026) are a past event and are used only for last_sign_of_life. The newsletter sign up on the site shows a setup error. The Hamlet page names Revolution Shakespeare as a presenting partner; see leads_only.

records.name: Nice Roots Farm (SHARE Food Program)
records.summary: The farm of SHARE Food Program, which grows fresh fruit and vegetables for donation to the community, to SHARE-affiliated pantries, and to mutual aid networks. Volunteers can sign up on the program's page.
records.what_you_do: Join a Community Farming Day from May through December to prep beds, plant and seed, weed and water, mulch, harvest, and clean up the grounds. Food rescues are also claimed in the Philly Food Rescue app.

schedule.text: Community Farming Days run May through December. Food rescues are claimed in the app as they come up, and each takes about an hour or less.

locations.label: SHARE Food Program office (the farm sits beside the Share Warehouse in Allegheny West; farm street address not published)

requirements.gear: Closed-toe shoes or boots, clothes you can get dirty, a water bottle, and garden gloves if you have them.

first_step.how: Click the Volunteer to Help button on the farm's page to sign up for a Community Farming Day. Food rescues are claimed separately in the Philly Food Rescue app.
first_step.basis: Anyone of any age can sign up through a clear button, and the page lists the tasks and what to bring. It does not say whether beginners are welcome or how a first day runs.
first_step.what_to_expect: A Community Farming Day is fully outdoors, so the weather matters, and the page advises checking the forecast the day before. The farm manager, Ellie Kaplan, runs the farm year-round with help from others. The page does not give a start time or how long a day lasts.
first_visit_tips: Wear closed-toe shoes or boots and clothes you do not mind getting dirty.
Check the forecast the day before and dress in layers, since the work is outdoors.
Bring sun protection, and take care if you are bothered by mosquitoes or stings.
For food rescues, you need a cell phone and must be able to lift at least 30 pounds, or bring a friend.

records.notes: This record covers two volunteer paths under one id: Nice Roots Farm (farm days, May to December) and Philly Food Rescue (app-claimed pickups, which need a phone and lifting; a driver's license and insurance only if you drive). The batch file calls the group 'Philly Food Rescue', but the record file calls it 'Nice Roots Farm (SHARE Food Program)'; the record file name is kept. The orchestrator may want to split the record. The farm pages give no farm street address; the office address on the page is used with a label that says so. No accessibility information appears on the farm pages. The only year tied to the farm is 2010 (its start). Ellie Kaplan's direct email is on the farming page; the general volunteer address is used. Commitment changed from drop_in to seasonal to match the farm days.

records.name: SHARP Dance Company
records.summary: A modern dance company in Philadelphia that tells stories through movement. Students can take its dance classes or its summer dance intensive, and anyone can see its shows.
records.what_you_do: Take the Monday open company class for $10, or buy a ticket to a show. Company auditions are closed for now.

schedule.text: Open company classes run every Monday from 10 to 11 am. The company also runs summer dance intensives; the 2026 ones were for ages 14 to 20 and for ages 18 and up.

locations.label: Equilibrium Dance Academy (Monday open company classes)
Company address listed on its contact page (street not published here)

cost.text: Monday open company classes are $10 per class, paid in cash or by Venmo on site. Show tickets are sold separately.

first_step.how: Go to the Monday 10 am open company class at Equilibrium Dance Academy, 1802 S. Broad Street. Sign the liability form on arrival and pay $10 on site. Email the company first if you want to know the class level.
first_step.basis: The Monday classes are open to the public, need no registration, and cost $10 a class, so the way in is clear. The page does not say the class level or whether beginners are welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each open company class runs one hour, from 10 to 11 am on Mondays, at Equilibrium Dance Academy on South Broad Street. You sign a liability form, pay $10 in cash or by Venmo, and take the class, and the page asks everyone to arrive on time. The company does not describe the level of the class, so email before your first visit if you are new to dance.
first_visit_tips: Arrive on time, since the page asks everyone to.
Bring cash or the Venmo app for the $10 fee.
Sign the liability form before you take the class.
Email the company first to ask about level or beginners, because the site does not say.

records.notes: The id ends in '-copy' and the aka is 'SHARP Dance Company Copy'. No sharp-dance-company file exists under data/groups/s/, so no duplicate verdict was given; the orchestrator may want to fix the id. The contact page lists two emails: corpdancer@yahoo.com (kept, shown beside the artistic director's name) and sharpdancephila@gmail.com (listed under Contact Us). Calendar performances are one-time events and are left out of schedule. The calendar shows no year for the Doudna (Aug 29), Richmond (Oct 14) and FringeArts (Nov 13 and 14) dates, so no year is written for them; tier 1 had added 2026 to two of them. The NYC showcase is written as January 17, 2027. The company address on its contact page is a condominium building, so no street address is published.

records.name: SideQuest Theater
records.summary: An improv theater near Rittenhouse Square that offers a free intro workshop, eight-week improv classes from beginner to advanced, and its own shows.
records.what_you_do: Take the free intro workshop, sign up for an eight-week improv class, or come see one of the theater's own shows.

schedule.text: Improv series run eight weeks, on Monday and Thursday evenings from 7 to 9:30 pm, and each series ends with a student performance for friends and family.

cost.text: Improv series are $399 for eight weeks. The free intro workshop costs nothing. Show tickets are sold separately.

access.notes: Nearest SEPTA stop, per the theater's FAQ: the 19th Street trolley station, a short walk. Bus routes 9, 12, 17, 21 and 42 also stop nearby.

first_step.how: Register for the free 90 minute Intro to Improv workshop through the link on the classes page, or ask the theater by email or phone about the next eight-week beginner class (Improv 1). Registration runs through linked sites.
first_step.basis: The site labels a free 90 minute intro workshop as beginner friendly, says improv is for everyone, and lists a beginner eight-week class with a clear way to register.
first_step.what_to_expect: Improv 1 is the beginner series: eight Thursday evenings from 7 to 9:30 pm, starting with the basics and ending with a short two person scene. Classes are for people 18 and up unless a class is marked for minors, and each series ends with a performance for friends and family. Each series costs $399, so the free intro workshop is a no-cost way to try improv first.
first_visit_tips: Start with the free intro workshop if you are unsure, since the site labels it beginner friendly.
Buy show tickets ahead; only a limited number are sold at the door, and you can give your name at the box office with no printed ticket.
Parking: Park America (2027 Sansom St) and Patriot Parking (2102 Sansom St) are the closest lots, and street parking is not guaranteed.
The theater is BYO, so you can bring your own drinks. Some shows are for adults only, so check the rating on the Shows page first.

records.notes: Tier 1 summary had 'October 2 to 25, 2026', but the site writes Camp Dread's dates with no year, so the year was removed from the summary. The 2026-10 last sign of life is carried from tier 1 and is not backed by a written 2026 date on the pages read; the newest year written is 2027 (January enrollment for Improv 1). The Improv 1 register button says June to August while the listed dates say January to March, so confirm which session is open. Improv 2 and 3 show no year. Two workshops (Improv for RPGs and Improv for GMs) have no dates yet. The accessibility statement page loaded only its navigation, so no accessibility features are confirmed.
